skill.description: Inspect bounded text, files, records, URLs, lists, and skill packets for duplicates while preserving provenance and separating mutation from analysis.
skill.summary: Create evidence-rich duplicate reports before any approved cleanup.

remediation.suggestion: Add configurable hard limits and reject oversized requests before reading files or starting pairwise similarity comparisons.

semantic_findings.title: Unenforced Input Bounds Can Exhaust Resources
semantic_findings.description: The inspector accepts arrays without size limits, then performs pairwise text similarity comparisons. Large inputs can consume excessive CPU and memory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The request array has no enforced maximum, and the nested comparison loops are directly visible. Runtime growth is quadratic for text similarity.

content.value_statement: Duplicate cleanup can remove unique information when identity rules are unclear. This skill creates evidence-rich reports and gates every mutation behind explicit review.
actual_capabilities: Groups exact and normalized duplicates across text, file, record, URL, list, and skill adapters.
Computes SHA-256 evidence for file contents, comparison keys, and complete skill packets.
Reports pairwise text similarity candidates without treating them as confirmed duplicates.
Identifies conflicting non-key fields inside record groups.
Normalizes URL components only through declared policies and without network requests.
Emits canonical indices, unresolved items, provenance, and reconciled counts.
limitations: The bundled command only inspects data and does not execute mutation plans.
Requests must provide a bounded JSON array and explicit identity policies.
Similarity scoring supports text only and uses Python SequenceMatcher.
The inspector does not resolve URL redirects or contact network services.

use_cases.title: Review Duplicate Exports
use_cases.description: Inspect repeated customer or inventory records while preserving conflicting fields for review.

use_cases.title: Compare File Collections
use_cases.description: Find byte-identical or normalized text files and retain paths, hashes, and unresolved links.

use_cases.title: Audit Skill Installations
use_cases.description: Compare complete skill packets and separate exact duplicates from same-name conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Find Exact List Duplicates
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this bounded list for exact duplicates. Keep the first item, report canonical indices, and do not mutate the source: [items].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a small list using exact identity.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize Text Before Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect these text items using NFKC, case folding, and collapsed whitespace. Separate normalized matches from similarity candidates: [items].
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare text that may differ by formatting or Unicode representation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Record Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect these records using [key fields] as normalized identity. Report every conflicting non-key field and propose a canonical map without changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a record merge review while preserving unique values.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Verified File Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect these bounded file paths using byte identity. Produce provenance, duplicate groups, unresolved links, a canonical plan, and verification requirements without deleting anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare an advanced cleanup plan with evidence and mutation controls.

output_examples.input: Inspect a list containing Alpha, Alpha, and Beta with exact identity.
output_examples.output: The report keeps the first Alpha and Beta, identifies the second Alpha as one duplicate, and confirms that no source item changed.

output_examples.input: Compare two customer records by normalized email while their names and identifiers differ.
output: One normalized duplicate group links both source indices.
The name and identifier fields remain listed as unresolved conflicts.
The report proposes the first record as canonical without applying changes.

output_examples.input: Compare two similar text passages with a score threshold of 0.90.
output_examples.output: The report lists the pair and score as a similarity candidate. Both passages remain canonical because similarity is not identity.

best_practices: Define scope, identity class, normalization, and canonical selection before inspection.
Review conflicts and unresolved items before authorizing any mutation plan.
Rerun inspection after approved changes and reconcile every source count.
anti_patterns: Do not treat similarity scores as confirmed identity.
Do not remove files or records from a generic cleanup request.
Do not hide lossy normalization or discard conflicting fields.

faq.question: Does this skill delete duplicate files?
faq.answer: No. The bundled inspector is read-only and only produces reports. A separate host capability must apply an explicitly approved plan.

faq.question: Which collection types are supported?
faq.answer: It supports text, files, records, URLs, lists, and skill directories.

faq.question: Can it find similar text?
faq.answer: Yes. It reports pairwise SequenceMatcher scores above an explicit threshold. It keeps those pairs separate from duplicate groups.

faq.question: Does URL comparison use the network?
faq.answer: No. URL normalization is local. Redirect resolution requires separate network authority and is not implemented by the inspector.

faq.question: How are canonical items selected?
faq.answer: The inspector reports the first resolved item in each equality group. Operational cleanup should use the reviewed canonical policy.

faq.question: How are unreadable files or invalid items handled?
faq.answer: They appear as unresolved items with source indices and reasons. They are excluded from duplicate counts instead of being silently dropped.
